historical_growth.basis: Continuing operations from FY2022 to avoid the Qualtrics break: revenue FY2022 29,520 continuing (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2023.txt:9605) -> FY2025 36,800; FY2020 27,338 as reported (includes Qualtrics, ~EUR 0.7bn) for the 5yr. EPS diluted continuing: FY2022 2.79 -> FY2025 6.10 (kpis EPSContinuing), FY2020 4.35. Equity FY2022 40,186 / FY2020 29,717 -> FY2025 44,586. Owner FCF = OCF - capex - SBC: FY2025 6,722; FY2022 3,342 (4,773 - continuing SBC 1,431, SAP.DE_Annual_FY2023.txt:9950); FY2020 5,294.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 3.5% vs revenue 7.6% and continuing EPS 29.8%: book value is held down by the EUR 3.2bn 2024 restructuring, ~EUR 2.7bn/yr dividends and ~EUR 2bn/yr buybacks, so it is not a usable growth proxy. Continuing EPS 3yr is off a depressed FY2022 (venture write-downs) and the FY2024 restructuring trough, and overstates the run-rate. Revenue 3yr CAGR 7.6% is the cleanest anchor; the base path starts above it (10%) on FY2026 guidance and the +26% current cloud backlog and converges below it by year 8.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 4.9% vs reported 5.7%: SBC grew from EUR 1,084m (FY2020) to EUR 1,695m (FY2025; peak 2,385m in FY2024), faster than cash flow, so part of the reported growth was paid for in stock-linked compensation. The 3yr owner-FCF figure (26%) is flattered by the FY2022 base (Qualtrics, restructuring) and the FY2025 first clean post-restructuring year.

scenario_narratives.base: SAP converts the bulk of its ECC base to S/4HANA Cloud through the Dec-2027 maintenance cliff: cloud grows ~25% in FY2026 (Q3 +26%, guidance toward the top of EUR 25.8-26.2bn) and stays above 15% through FY2028 while support and licences shrink to a remainder, so total revenue compounds ~10% for two years then decelerates to GDP-plus by year 8. The EUR 24.1bn current cloud backlog underwrites the first two years. Operating leverage arrives as management frames it (opex at 80-90% of revenue growth in 2027), taking pre-SBC EBITDA from 34.5% to 41% by FY2032 but no faster, because cloud mix dilutes gross margin and SAP keeps buying data/AI capability (Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs) to stay credible in agentic workflows. Business AI/Joule and Business Data Cloud expand wallet share modestly rather than transformatively. The EU commitments case, DOJ inquiry and Celonis trial cost money and management time but do not change the maintenance model.
scenario_narratives.bull: The migration wave is larger and stickier than the base assumes: SI capacity holds, AI-assisted migration tooling cuts conversion effort, and the ECC customers who had not started by 2025 overwhelmingly stay with SAP rather than defecting to Oracle Fusion or Workday. Business AI/BDC becomes a priced layer on top of core ERP, so cloud growth holds above 20% into FY2028 and total revenue compounds 11-12% for three years. Margins expand ~1.5pp/yr to a 44% pre-SBC EBITDA plateau as AI tooling costs normalise and internal AI deployment lowers S&M, R&D and G&A ratios. Deferred-revenue capture runs at 15% on stronger bookings and terminal growth is 3.0%. The SaaS-disruption narrative proves wrong for systems-of-record ERP, where seats are not the pricing unit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Agentic AI compresses per-seat SaaS economics industry-wide and SAP's cloud pricing power erodes; SI bottlenecks ahead of 2027 push a meaningful minority of ECC customers to extended maintenance, third-party support (helped by the EU Commission commitments opening on-premise maintenance) or to Oracle/Workday/Microsoft, so cloud growth fades to the low teens by FY2028 while the legacy decline accelerates as guided. Total revenue growth falls from 9% to 3% within four years. The AI investment phase is not temporary: margins stall near 37% pre-SBC EBITDA, SBC stays at 4.6% of revenue, and continued bolt-on M&A dilutes further. Terminal growth 2.0% and a 15x cap reflect a mature, slower franchise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SAP is valued as a stream of owner free cash flow in EUR -- SBC charged once at the IFRS 2 expense, leases as an operating cost, share count flat at the diluted 1,175m, WACC built from Bund yields -- against the Xetra price in EUR. The business is a high-switching-cost systems-of-record franchise mid-way through a forced on-premise-to-cloud migration that ends in Dec-2027, so the near-term path is unusually visible (EUR 24bn current cloud backlog, guidance) and the long-term question is what the franchise earns once migration is done and whether agentic AI changes enterprise software pricing. Scenarios differ on how much of the ECC base SAP keeps, where pre-SBC margins plateau (37% / 41% / 44%), and the terminal growth and cap that follow. One discount rate across all scenarios; risk is in the weights and the flows. Driver paths are shared with the SAP NYSE ADR valuation so the two listings read consistently.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin plateau: each 1pp of mature pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly EUR 4-5/share; management held rather than raised FY2026 profit guidance after the Q3 beat
Terminal value is the majority of EV at an 8.5% WACC; 1pp of WACC or 0.5pp of terminal growth moves base value by double digits (see sensitivity grid)

Balance-sheet anchors are FY2025 (2025-12-31); 2026 acquisitions, the Teradata settlement, dividend and buybacks are only partly reflected via equity_bridge until the H1/Q3-2026 interim reports are extracted

SBC mechanics: awards are largely cash-settled and marked to market, so the IFRS 2 expense (and the 4.5% charge) swings with the share price -- after the ~17% rally since early October the FY2026 expense will run higher than the path's start
EUR strength: SAP reports in EUR with a majority of revenue outside the eurozone; a stronger euro lowers reported revenue and FCF even when constant-currency growth is on plan
Regulatory outcomes (EU Commission commitments, DOJ, Celonis) could force changes to maintenance and data-access practices that the bear case only partly prices

data_sources.financials: research/SAP.DE/Reports/SAP.DE_Metrics.csv and SAP.DE.duckdb kpis (FY2014-FY2025 annual plus interims), with anchors read from the extracted FY2025 and FY2023 annual reports (file:line cited per field).

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2025 weighted average shares outstanding, diluted, 1,175m (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:15412; basic 1,166m + 9m dilutive effect of share-based payments, treasury stock excluded). The NumberOfSharesIssued figure of 1,229m includes ~62m treasury shares and is not used. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; SAP's repurchases (EUR 1,916m FY2025, EUR 10bn programme announced Feb-2026) are the cash mechanism funding the flat count and are value-neutral here. The SAP (NYSE ADR) sibling valuation of 2026-10-04 used 1,167m (basic, implied from NI/EPS, no filing text available); this build corrects to the diluted figure read off the filing.
inputs.net_debt_note: SAP's own net liquidity at 2025-12-31 (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:4029-4041): cash and cash equivalents 8,220 + current time deposits and debt securities 1,311 = group liquidity 9,531, less financial debt 6,150 (bonds 5,650 + commercial paper 500, bank loans 0) = net liquidity 3,381. Lease liabilities (1,684) excluded under lease treatment (B). The current time deposits/debt securities are included because their interest is outside the flows (see interest_income); the SAP ADR sibling counted cash only (net cash 2,070).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF continuing 9,156 - purchases of intangibles and PP&E 739 (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:3075-3079). SAP's own FCF definition is 8,239 after +121 asset-sale proceeds and -299 lease principal; the lease cost is charged in the forward build via lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero by construction, not by materiality: effective 2025 SAP no longer classifies interest received (FY2025 EUR 420m) or interest paid (EUR 574m) in operating cash flow (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:2872, 13073), so reported FCF is already ex-interest income and the 9,531 group liquidity is added once in the bridge without double counting.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, share-based payment expense EUR 1,695m (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:12994; FY2024 2,385, FY2023 2,220). SAP publishes no separate equity-award tax line and no combined figure; awards are predominantly cash-settled, so the add-back is used unadjusted and EquityAwardTaxes is 0 in kpis.
inputs.buyback_note: Purchase of treasury shares FY2025 EUR 1,916m (SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:12960); FY2024 2,108. SAP is a repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not merely a convention.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:26Z Xetra regular close (Friday; valuation dated Sunday 2026-10-25, no newer session)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of both the flows and the Xetra quote: 10y Bund ~2.7%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.1 (large-cap software) gives cost of equity ~8.2%; SAP is funded almost entirely by equity (EUR 6.15bn financial debt against EUR 9.5bn liquidity) so WACC ~= cost of equity, rounded up to 8.5%. One rate across all three scenarios -- risk is charged in the probability-weighted flows. Identical to the SAP ADR sibling so the two listings are comparable.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease charge 1.0% of revenue inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (FY2025 payments of lease liabilities EUR 299m principal plus lease interest, ~0.9-1.0% of revenue; SAP.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt:3079). D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation: total D&A 1,311 less ROU depreciation 275 (line 16282) = 1,036 = 2.8% of revenue. Lease liabilities (1,684) excluded from net debt. Check: adj EBITDA 34.5% - SBC 4.6% - lease ~1.0% - D&A ex-ROU 2.8% = 26.1% = FY2025 IFRS operating margin (9,617 / 36,800).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests EUR 488m at FY2025 (~1% of equity, line 12870) and immaterial to earnings since the Qualtrics divestiture; attributable and consolidated flows treated as identical, no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 2: non-US operating company, enterprise software, with the lease and currency adaptations; currency and quote currency are both EUR so no FX bridge). FIRST VALUATION OF SAP.DE, but the same company was valued 2026-10-04 through its NYSE ADR (research/SAP, 1 ADR = 1 share, EUR flows bridged to USD). That build's scenario driver paths, weights, WACC and terminal assumptions are adopted UNCHANGED here so the two listings stay comparable; see sibling_crosscheck for the EUR bridge. What differs is anchors only, now read off the extracted FY2025 annual report (which the ADR build did not have): diluted share count 1,175m (was 1,167m), net liquidity 3,381 including current deposits (was 2,070 cash-only net), price in EUR. NEW EVIDENCE SINCE 2026-10-04: Q3-2026 results (2026-10-21): cloud revenue +26% to EUR 6.67bn, current cloud backlog +26% cc to EUR 24.14bn (vs +27% at Q2 -- the 'slightly decelerate' FY2026 guidance playing out), non-IFRS operating profit +18% to EUR 3.03bn, total quarterly revenue above EUR 10bn for the first time; cloud guidance moved toward the upper end of EUR 25.8-26.2bn, non-IFRS OP held at EUR 11.8-12.2bn (trimmed in July for Dremio/Prior Labs dilution), FCF ~EUR 10bn maintained. FY2026 GROWTH RE-JUDGED AND LEFT AT 10.0%: upper-end cloud ~EUR 26.1bn + support ~EUR 9.7bn (-8%) + licences ~EUR 0.7bn + services ~EUR 4.3bn = ~EUR 40.8bn, +10.9% cc, less ~1pp reported FX headwind from the stronger 2026 euro on SAP's USD revenue = ~10% reported; the Q3 beat moves the cc figure by a few tenths, inside that FX uncertainty. FY2026 margin left at 36.5% because OP guidance was held, not raised. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED (all scenarios): FY2027+ growth, the 41%/44%/37% margin plateaus, SBC % paths, 27% cash tax, 2.0% capex, 10/15/5% working-capital capture, terminal growth and caps, 20/50/30 weights. What would move them: FY2027 guidance at the January 2027 Q4 print (growth years 2-3), any change to the 80-90% opex-to-revenue-growth framework (margin path), the EU Commission commitments decision and the Dec-2026 Celonis trial (bear weight), and SBC settling below ~4% of revenue for two years (SBC path). ANCHOR VINTAGE: balance sheet and share count are FY2025 (2025-12-31); H1-2026 and Q3-2026 interim reports are not extracted for this ticker. 2026 cash movements: May dividend EUR 2.35/sh (~EUR 2.7bn) and buybacks against ~EUR 7bn+ of 9M FCF, net roughly offsetting; the three disclosed acquisition/settlement outflows are deducted in equity_bridge. Year-1 (FY2026) flows are discounted a full year although ~75% of the year has elapsed -- a conservative timing convention shared with the sibling and the rest of the folder. FCF: SAP's interest reclassification from 2025 means reported FCF needs no interest-income strip (see interest_income_note). SBC SETTLEMENT CAVEAT: SAP's awards are largely cash-settled and that cash is inside OCF, so last_fcf (reported FCF - SBC expense) double-counts the cash-settled portion for FY2025; the forward build is unaffected because adj EBITDA is pre-SBC and the IFRS 2 expense is charged once via sbc_pct_path.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +10% (re-judged after Q3-2026, unchanged): upper-end cloud ~EUR 26.1bn cc + support ~EUR 9.7bn + licences ~EUR 0.7bn + services ~EUR 4.3bn = ~EUR 40.8bn, +10.9% cc, less ~1pp reported FX headwind. FY2027 +10% on the +26% current cloud backlog, management's 'accelerate through 2027' total-revenue guidance and the Dec-2027 ECC maintenance cliff. Decelerates from FY2028 as the forced-migration wave passes and support shrinks to a remainder; 3.5% by year 10, 1pp above terminal.
base.margin_rationale: adj EBITDA is pre-SBC, pre-lease, IFRS-16 basis. FY2025 actual 34.5% (IFRS OP 26.1% + SBC 4.6% + D&A 3.6% incl. ROU). FY2026 36.5% backed out of guidance: non-IFRS OP EUR 12.0bn mid on ~EUR 40.5bn = 29.6%, less ~1.2pp acquisition-related/restructuring to IFRS OP ~28.4%, plus SBC 4.5% and D&A ~3.6%. Expansion ~1pp/yr to 41% by FY2032, consistent with SAP's 2027 framework of opex growing at 80-90% of revenue growth, and still below Oracle/Microsoft because cloud gross margin (~75%) dilutes support (~90%).
base.tax_rationale: IFRS effective tax rate 28.7% FY2025, non-IFRS ~29% guided for 2026; cash taxes paid EUR 2,198m FY2025 (~24% of pre-tax). 27% flat on positive EBIT; no NOLs to ramp from.
base.wc_rationale: Cloud subscriptions are billed in advance (contract liabilities EUR 6.7bn FY2025, +EUR 0.66bn YoY); 10% capture of the YoY revenue increase is the conservative end of the prepaid-SaaS range because receivables and the shrinking prepaid support base partly offset.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from the SAP ADR sibling (2026-10-04). Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the regulatory overhang is unusually broad -- EU Commission maintenance proceeding, DOJ inquiry, Celonis trial Dec-2026 -- and all of it targets the practices that keep the installed base captive, while AI-driven SaaS repricing is a live market narrative. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs SI capacity, AI monetisation at scale and margin expansion beyond guidance to all go right. Base 50%: the ECC cliff is a time-boxed, largely captive tailwind and the backlog is already booked; Q3-2026 confirmed the base path rather than moving weight toward bull.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
